- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly, especially after sharp drops.
- After a large spike in price (true outcome > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5–10% above peak or adjust downward after 2–3 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending sideways, model often drifts toward mean; apply mean reversion bias toward recent 7–14 day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early volatility (first 5–7 days), model often misses it; adjust upward if sentiment turns bullish early, downward if bearish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model may lag; add 1–2 day lag correction to forecast.
- When sentiment is flat (all 0.00 or 0.67) and price is stable, model often drifts; apply smoothing or decay factor to reduce forecast drift.
